hook.line: Most of the neighbours voted, a group of tourists arrived, half of them left. In English you pick a verb by feel. In Spanish, a few words like these leave you a real choice, and native speakers use both.
hook.es: La mayoría de los vecinos votó en contra.
hook.en: Most of the neighbours voted against.

examples.es: La mayoría de los vecinos votó en contra.
examples.en: Most of the neighbours voted against.

examples.es: La mayoría de los vecinos votaron en contra.
examples.en: Most of the neighbours voted against.

examples.es: La mitad de los vecinos se fue temprano.
examples.en: Half of the neighbours left early.

rule:
Some nouns look singular but stand for many people: *la mayoría*, *un grupo*, *la gente*, *la mitad*. Which verb do you use?

With *la mayoría de* or *un grupo de* plus a plural noun, you have a choice. Strict grammar says the verb agrees with the singular head: *la mayoría votó*. But because the meaning is plural, *votaron* is common too, and both are correct.

The choice is stylistic: the singular is more formal, the plural more natural when you picture the people one by one.

*La gente* is always singular in Spanish: *la gente quiere*, not *quieren*. English "people" is plural, so watch this one.

*La mitad* (half) behaves like *la mayoría*: *la mitad se fue* or *se fueron*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this agreement *ad sensum*, agreement by meaning: the verb follows the sense rather than the strict grammar.

readAndPick.es: La mayoría de los vecinos votó en contra.
options: Most of the neighbours voted against.
A few neighbours voted against.
No neighbour voted against.
Some tourists left.
A group of tourists arrived.
A tourist arrived.
The people wanted tea.
People want coffee.
I want coffee for the people.

readAndPick.es: La mitad de los vecinos se fue temprano.
options: Half of the neighbours left early.
The rest arrived late.
He rested early.

readAndPick.es: La mayoría de los clientes pidió tinto.
options: Most of the customers asked for black coffee.
None of the customers asked for black coffee.
The customer asked for black coffee.

readAndPick.es: Un grupo de niños jugaban afuera.
options: A child was playing outside.
A group of children were playing outside.
The children will play outside.

readAndPick.es: La gente habla mucho en este barrio.
options: The people spoke a lot in that neighbourhood.
I talk a lot in this neighbourhood.
People talk a lot in this neighbourhood.

readAndPick.es: La mitad de los vecinos no vino.
options: Half of the neighbours didn't come.
The neighbours rested and didn't come.
The rest of the neighbours came.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the verb and type the whole sentence: *La mayoría de los vecinos ___ en contra.* (votó or votaron)
yourTurn.answer: La mayoría de los vecinos votó en contra.
accept: La mayoría de los vecinos votaron en contra.
yourTurn.why: Both work: singular follows the grammar, plural follows the meaning.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: A group of tourists arrived.
Type in Spanish: People want coffee.
yourTurn.why: *La gente* is always singular in Spanish, so the verb is *quiere*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Half of the neighbours left early.
yourTurn.answer: La mitad de los vecinos se fue temprano.
accept: La mitad de los vecinos se fueron temprano.
yourTurn.why: *La mitad* works like *la mayoría*: *se fue* is the strict form, *se fueron* is common.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Most of the customers asked for black coffee.
yourTurn.answer: La mayoría de los clientes pidió tinto.
accept: La mayoría de los clientes pidieron tinto.
yourTurn.why: With *la mayoría de*, singular and plural are both correct.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about the past: *La gente habla mucho en este barrio.* Say: People talked a lot in this neighbourhood.
yourTurn.answer: La gente habló mucho en este barrio.
yourTurn.why: *La gente* stays singular, so the past is *habló*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Half of the neighbours didn't come.
yourTurn.answer: La mitad de los vecinos no vino.
accept: La mitad de los vecinos no vinieron.
yourTurn.why: The singular head *la mitad* allows *vino*, and *vinieron* would be fine too.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English "people" is plural, but *la gente* is singular in Spanish.

pitfalls.wrong: Los mayoría de los vecinos votó en contra.
pitfalls.right: La mayoría de los vecinos votó en contra.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Mayoría* is a feminine noun, so it takes *la*.

pitfalls.wrong: La mayoría de la gente quieren café.
pitfalls.right: La mayoría de la gente quiere café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. With *la gente* after *de*, nothing in the phrase is plural, so the verb stays singular.

personal: Tell me what most of your friends or neighbours do, starting with *La mayoría de* and picking a singular or plural verb.
